title: Observability: integrate anomaly detection pipelines and refine paging policies for SLO coverage
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: improve early detection of SLO regressions and reduce noisy pages by wiring anomaly-detection signals into the metrics/logs pipeline, adding adaptive burn-rate windows, and clarifying pager escalation policies. This ticket covers pipeline changes (metrics + logs), dashboard updates for latency/error SLOs, integration tests for detection thresholds, and updating runbooks/playbooks for oncall. We will avoid increasing metric cardinality significantly and keep storage/cost impact within the Optimize budget.
acceptance_criteria: Anomaly detection job emits validated alerts into the existing alert stream with a clear mapping to SLOs (latency_p95, error_rate) and a documented false-positive rate < 5% in canary region
Burn-rate alerts for critical SLOs are added with two severity tiers (warning and paging) and respect scheduled quiet windows and maintenance flags
Dashboards updated: per-route latency heatmaps, sliding-window burn-rate visual, and anomaly overlays on the last 7 days
Pager policy updated and published: oncall rotation rules, escalation timeline, runbook links, and a playbook for handling anomaly-triggered pages
Integration tests validate trace hook propagation and metric labels across sampling levels and do not regress ingestion throughput by >10%
A staged rollout plan exists (canary -> cross-region -> global) with rollback criteria and automated smoke checks
implementation_notes: Add an aggregation layer job that consumes prom-style metrics + structured logs, computes windowed burn-rate and anomaly scores using median absolute deviation + EWMA baseline
Instrument tracing hooks to carry route_id, customer_tier, and request_priority without adding high-cardinality tag explosion; use hashed tags for optional dimensions
Use existing alert bus (pagerduty/routing) and add a new 'anomaly-slo' routing key so teams can opt into or mute anomaly sources
Introduce a configurable threshold tuner that can relax thresholds for low-traffic routes to avoid noisy behaviour
Work with Cost Ops to estimate storage/compute cost of new detectors; constrain to Optimize project budget and provide mitigation options (sample, downsample, TTL)
testing_plan: Create synthetic traffic generator to simulate ramping latency and error bursts; verify detection and burn-rate calculation correctness
Canary in us-west-2 for 48h validating false-positive rate and runbook execution with simulated page acknowledgements
Load test metrics ingestion to ensure CPU/memory within limits; failure modes must degrade to passive logging only (no paging) if pipeline backpressure detected
Unit tests for trace hook propagation and label normalization; e2e smoke tests for dashboard rendering and alert firing
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Deploy detectors and dashboards to canary region (us-west-2) for 48-72h
Phase 2: Open beta for selected internal teams + monitoring for 7 days; gather fp/fn metrics
Phase 3: Gradual expansion to all regions with configuration toggles per workspace
Fallback: disable anomaly routing or revert to static burn-rate thresholds if FP rate > 10% or missed pages > 5%
